technical.lead: Microsoft Scout ships as an always-on work agent built on OpenClaw
technical.body: Microsoft used its Build keynote this week to introduce Scout, an always-on personal agent it frames as its first "Autopilot" - a class of agent that runs continuously, holds its own identity, and acts on the user's behalf rather than waiting for a sidebar prompt. Scout spans cloud, desktop, and web and plugs directly into Teams, Outlook, OneDrive, and SharePoint to read threads, pull data, draft documents, schedule meetings, and chase tasks across those apps, per the [Microsoft 365 Blog - Introducing Microsoft Scout: Your always-on personal agent](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/blog/2026/06/02/introducing-microsoft-scout-your-always-on-personal-agent/). The substance for this brief is what it runs on: Scout is powered by OpenClaw, the open-source local-agent platform, wrapped in Microsoft enterprise controls - every agent runs under a governed Entra identity with scoped credentials, audit trails, a continuous policy-conformance check, and Purview data-protection enforcement before data leaves, plus a Work IQ context layer. Availability is narrow at launch: an internal desktop build is now extended to select customers in private preview through the Frontier early-access program, gated behind Frontier enrollment, Intune policy, an opt-in attestation, and a GitHub Copilot license, with a broader waitlisted preview expected later in 2026, per [Thurrott - Build 2026: Microsoft Unveils New 'Scout' Personal Work Agent Powered by OpenClaw](https://www.thurrott.com/a-i/336926/build-2026-microsoft-unveils-scout-personal-work-agent-and-new-in-house-ai-models). The throughline is that one of the three open coding/agent harnesses this brief tracks is now the engine inside a first-party Microsoft product placed directly inside Teams and Outlook as a participant.

technical.lead: Nvidia posts Nemotron 3 Ultra 550B open weights, top US open model
technical.body: The Nemotron 3 Ultra weights Jensen Huang previewed at Computex on June 1 went live today on Hugging Face. Nvidia's Nemotron v3 collection now lists the 550-billion-parameter Ultra in three freshly uploaded variants - an instruction-tuned BF16 build, a Base-BF16 pretrained checkpoint, and an NVFP4 quantized build - alongside a generative reward model, per the [Hugging Face - NVIDIA Nemotron v3 collection](https://huggingface.co/collections/nvidia/nvidia-nemotron-v3). The model is a mixture-of-experts design with roughly 55 billion parameters active per token, a 1-million-token context window, and a claimed 300-plus tokens per second of output, positioned as the first open model built from the ground up for multi-step agent reasoning rather than chat. On the independent Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index it scores 48, the strongest US open-weights model released to date and ahead of every other American open model - though it still trails China's Kimi K2.6 at 54, so the "best open model" claim holds only within the US field, per [Implicator.ai - Nvidia's Nemotron 3 Ultra leads US open models but trails China's Kimi K2.6](https://www.implicator.ai/nvidias-nemotron-3-ultra-leads-us-open-models-but-trails-chinas-kimi-k2-6/). The catch is hardware: a 550B model needs datacenter-class memory to self-host, so most teams reach it through hosted endpoints, and the open release doubles as a funnel toward Nvidia silicon. For local builders the more runnable pieces are the smaller Nano (4B/30B) and Super (120B) members of the same v3 family, which the quantized formats make tractable on single-node hardware.

technical.lead: Surface RTX Spark Dev Box puts a 1-petaflop superchip on the desk
technical.body: Microsoft turned the RTX Spark superchip - the Nvidia/MediaTek Grace-Blackwell part unveiled at GTC Taipei this month - into a developer workstation, announcing the Surface RTX Spark Dev Box at Build. The deskside box pairs a Blackwell RTX GPU with a Grace CPU and 128 GB of unified memory for up to 1 petaflop of AI compute, enough to run 120B-plus-parameter models at a 1-million-token context entirely locally; it ships as a Secured-core PC running Windows 11 Pro with WSL 2 pre-configured for GPU passthrough and CUDA, VS Code, GitHub Copilot, and the AI Toolkit, managed through Entra ID and Intune, per the [Microsoft Devices Blog - Building the next generation of devices for developers: Surface RTX Spark Dev Box](https://blogs.windows.com/devices/2026/06/02/building-the-next-generation-of-devices-for-developers-surface-rtx-spark-dev-box/). It is listed as a pre-release device shipping later this year, exclusively through Microsoft.com. The relevant piece for embedded/edge local-LLM work is Foundry Local, Microsoft's on-device runtime - distinct from the Azure AI Foundry cloud marketplace - which reached general availability in April and shipped 1.1 and 1.2 updates at the end of May adding live audio transcription with a Nemotron ASR model, on-device text embeddings and Qwen 3.5 Vision multimodal inference, a downloadable WebGPU execution provider, Linux ARM64 support, and a bump to ONNX Runtime 1.26 across the Python, JavaScript, C#, and Rust SDKs, per [Microsoft Foundry Blog - What's new in Microsoft Foundry, May 2026](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/foundry/whats-new-in-microsoft-foundry-may-2026/). Together they describe Microsoft's local-AI pitch: a curated on-device runtime in a roughly 20 MB native library, paired with first-party hardware sized to run frontier-class open models off the cloud.

technical.lead: SpaceX fixes its IPO at $135 a share, a $1.77T listing
technical.body: SpaceX set a fixed $135-per-share price for its initial public offering ahead of the investor roadshow - unusual, since most issuers leave the number open until marketing finishes - in what would be the largest IPO in US history. At $135 the company sells about 555.5 million shares to raise roughly $75 billion at a valuation near $1.77 trillion, which would rank it among the most valuable US companies and above Tesla; the listing targets Nasdaq under the ticker SPCX, with pricing expected June 11 and a debut as soon as June 12, and Elon Musk retaining more than 85% of voting power through a dual-class structure despite about 42% of the economics, underwritten by a syndicate led by Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley, per [Stocktwits - SpaceX IPO Pricing At $135 Per Share Will Value The Rocket Maker At $1.77 Trillion](https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/spacex-ipo-pricing-135-per-share-will-value-the-rocket-maker-at-1.77-trillion/cZ0jlpNReUn). The print lands inside a crowded queue of AI-adjacent listings: Anthropic confirmed last week it has confidentially filed a draft S-1 with the SEC after a May round valued it at $965 billion (up from $380 billion in February), and OpenAI is reported to be preparing its own confidential filing in the coming weeks, per [Investing.com - Anthropic files confidentially for IPO in major AI industry milestone](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/anthropic-files-confidentially-for-ipo-in-major-ai-industry-milestone-4719863). The combined effect is that the year's biggest demands on public-market capital are now concentrated in companies whose theses rest on compute - rockets, frontier models, and the data centers behind them - testing whether equity markets can absorb that much AI-correlated supply at once.

technical.lead: With Build and Snowflake wrapped, WWDC, Databricks, AIE World's Fair next
technical.body: The dense early-June San Francisco conference run has closed out - Microsoft Build (Fort Mason, June 2-3) and Snowflake Summit 26 (Moscone, June 1-4) have both ended - and the still-upcoming calendar to plan attendance around starts with Apple. Apple WWDC26 runs Monday-Friday June 8-12 at Apple Park, with the keynote and Platforms State of the Union on Monday June 8 (keynote 10:00 AM PT), per [Apple Developer - WWDC26](https://developer.apple.com/wwdc26/). Databricks Data + AI Summit follows Monday-Thursday June 15-18 across Moscone with 800-plus sessions spanning data engineering, governance, analytics, applications, and agents, per [Moscone Center - Databricks Data + AI Summit 2026](https://www.moscone.com/events/databricks-data-ai-summit-2026). The AI Engineer World's Fair runs at Moscone West with New Engineer Orientation and badge pickup on Sunday June 28 (Day 0) and the main program Monday June 29 through Thursday July 2 - 29 tracks, 300-plus speakers, and 6,000-plus AI engineers, founders, and VPs of AI, per the [AI Engineer World's Fair 2026](https://www.ai.engineer/worldsfair/2026) site. For smaller local gatherings, AI Tinkerers SF keeps an active meetup calendar - recent and upcoming sessions have included an Advanced MCP Showcase, a Voice Agents Science Fair, and a GTM Engineering Track - with RSVPs through the chapter hub at [AI Tinkerers SF](https://sf.aitinkerers.org/). Further out, GitHub Universe returns to Fort Mason October 28-29, and AWS re:Invent runs November 30-December 4 in Las Vegas with registration opening June 16.

citations.label: Moscone Center - Databricks Data + AI Summit 2026
